when: Once per page load, after the page is interactive.
why: Which pages get opened, and from where: direct, internal, search, or external.

when: The disclosure strip under the masthead is at least 50 percent visible in the viewport.
why: Confirms the affiliate disclosure was actually on screen, not merely in the HTML. This is the compliance signal, measured.

when: A visitor clicks a Sponsored link to Amazon. The click is recorded and the browser navigates directly; nothing is intercepted or redirected.
why: Outbound intent per product. This is the only click metric the site can produce without Amazon reporting.

when: A visitor runs a search on this site.
why: The replacement for guessed keywords: the next guide topic is chosen from what visitors typed here, once an endpoint is live.

when: A guide page reaches 60 percent scroll depth, once per page view.
why: Distinguishes a guide that gets read from one that gets bounced, before more guides are written.
